newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran sees no need for OPEC ceiling rise.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees no need for OPEC ceiling rise.

text.p: Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Tuesday he did not believe that there was a need for OPEC countries to raise their output ceiling during talks in Vienna later this month.
"I think OPEC should be very careful about the ceiling for next year," he told Reuters on the sidelines of a news conference he held jointly with Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan.
"I don't think the current price will continue for a long time," he said.
Oil prices have dropped around $2.50 per barrel since hitting near six-year highs in mid-October.
He also said OPEC should closely monitor the outlook for supply and demand next year, but he did not elaborate.
OPEC, which meets in Vienna later this month, has a current output ceiling of 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd).
The group pumped around 25.86 million bpd in September, according to a Reuter survey.
